sections.name: File setup, mx
sections.title: Imports, map size and horizontal position
sections.what: Brings in the tools, the country center table, the colors and the helpers. Sets the drawing size to 960 by 520 units and provides the rule that turns a longitude into a horizontal position.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed drawing size keeps the background image and the markers aligned.
sections.watch_out: Changing the size without adjusting the background image and the vertical formula will misalign the markers.

sections.name: my, Pt
sections.title: Vertical position and point shape
sections.what: Turns a latitude into a vertical position using a flat-map method, limits latitudes to a range that avoids the poles, and moves the result by a fixed amount. Also defines the shape of a placed project point.
sections.why: Likely reason: the stretched vertical scale matches the background image. The fixed amount is not explained in the code; it likely lines the markers up with the image.
sections.watch_out: The fixed offset is a hand-set number, so a new background image will likely need a new value.

sections.name: PortfolioMap (part 1)
sections.title: Loading and grouping projects into markers
sections.what: Places each project using the location helper and counts exact, country-center and missing locations. Groups nearby exact sites into one marker, and groups each country's approximate points into their own marker. Each marker takes the most common phase among its projects and the list is sorted by size.
sections.why: The code comment says country points are grouped per country so they never merge with real sites.
sections.watch_out: The grouping cell shrinks as the user zooms in, so group keys change, and anything keyed on them, such as the selected group, can be lost.

sections.name: PortfolioMap (part 2)
sections.title: Zoom, pan and mouse handling
sections.what: Keeps zoom between 1 and 16 times, keeps the view inside the map edges, and turns mouse wheel, dragging and the zoom buttons into changes to the view. A drag is only treated as a drag once it moves more than a few units, so a click is not swallowed.
sections.why: Reason for the exact zoom limits of 1 and 16 is not stated in the code. The edge clamp keeps the map from being dragged off screen.
sections.watch_out: A very small movement counts as a click, so a slightly shaky press on a marker still selects it.

sections.name: PortfolioMap (part 3)
sections.title: Markers, labels, legend and selection panel
sections.what: Draws the background, grid lines, and country names once zoomed to three times or more. Draws a circle per marker, dashed for country points, with a count inside larger groups. Draws the phase legend, the source note for the map, and the side panel listing the projects in the selected group with a warning for country points.
sections.why: Likely reason: the legend and dashed outlines tell the reader how to tell real sites from approximate ones.
sections.watch_out: The dashed outline and the country warning protect against mistaking approximate locations for exact ones, so keep both if the marker style changes.

summary: An interactive world map that places each project as a marker, groups nearby ones, and lets the user zoom, pan and select.
purpose: Shows where projects are, separates exact site locations from approximate country center points, and lists the projects behind a selected marker.
why: Likely reason: country center points are drawn with a different style and a warning, so no one mistakes them for real sites.
how: Finds each project's location and sorts it into exact site, country center, or no location. Groups exact sites by a grid whose size depends on zoom, and groups country points by country. Draws the background map, grid lines, country names when zoomed in, and a circle per group, sized by count and colored by the most common phase. Handles mouse wheel zoom, dragging to pan, zoom buttons and selection by click or keyboard.
inputs: The list of projects, the industry name lookup, the location helper output, the country center table, and the background map image.
outputs: The map and its controls, counts of exact, approximate and missing locations, and a side panel listing the projects in the selected group. No data is changed.
risks: Groups are rebuilt as zoom changes, and selection is matched by a group key that depends on zoom, so a selected group can disappear when the user zooms. Country-center markers are not real sites, so the warning text is what prevents misreading. If the background image is missing, the map is blank but markers still show.
debug: If markers are missing, check the location counts; projects with no location are not drawn. If the map is blank, check the background image under the maps folder. If a click does nothing after a drag, that is the drag guard working as designed. If markers sit in the wrong place, check the position formulas and the fixed offset against the background image.
